identity.title: A single-nucleus multiome map of the human cerebellum with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.

content.abstract: Although cerebellum is neuropathologically affected in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-related dementia (ADRD), the cell type-specific genomic and epigenomic changes remain poorly understood. Here, we present single-nucleus multiome (RNA-seq and ATAC-seq) analysis of 103,861 nuclei isolated from both the cerebellum and frontal cortex of diseased individuals and cognitively healthy controls. We identify 431,834 significant peak-to-gene linkages across cell subtypes, revealing cis-regulatory elements linked to cell type-specific and disease-associated transcriptomic and regulatory network changes. Differential trajectory analysis pinpoints disease-associated genes in cerebellar granule cells, such as STMN1 and CLU. Integrating epigenomic, genetic, and three-dimensional genome data, we pinpoint two likely causal variants linked to SEZ6L2 in Purkinje cells and KANSL1 in granule cells. Through CRISPR interference in patient-derived cerebellar organoids, we show that silencing the variant-containing regulatory elements suppresses SEZ6L2 and KANSL1 expression, which perturbs neurodegeneration-associated gene programs. This cell type-specific regulatory landscape provides genomic and epigenomic insights into the pathological role of the cerebellum in AD/ADRD.
